subject: Request: key access justification + in-transit proof for SIG/CAIQ review
messages:
From: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@helix.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: SOC2 <soc2@helix.ai>, Tim Evans <tim.evans@bigbank.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: KMS/HSM evidence for SIG & CAIQ review

Hi Vanessa,

We're finishing the SIG/CAIQ review for Helix's integration and need a concise set of artifacts for your encryption and key management controls. The reviewers have asked for the following specific items (can you provide or point us to a package?):

- HSM attestation (vendor model, FIPS level, and date of attestation)
- Export of KMS rotation logs (last 12 months) with rotation event IDs and hashed key IDs
- Audit export of KMS access events covering create/get/wrap/unwrap (CSV or JSON)
- Description of envelope encryption approach (at-rest AES modes, key wrapping algorithm)
- Transit encryption proof: TLS cipher list, mTLS usage, and any load-balancer cert handling notes
- Key custody & access matrix showing RBAC, emergency access procedures, and break-glass logs
- Clarification on BYOK (customer key import) workflow if supported; example handshake artifacts preferred

We're on a tight timeline for SOC deliverables. If you can get an evidence bundle over by EOD Pacific tomorrow we can include it in the package to the auditor. If some items require an NDA or redaction, please flag what you can share.

Appreciate it — Alicia
Alicia Chen | Information Security, Helix AI
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: KMS/HSM evidence for SIG & CAIQ review

Folks — forwarding Helix's list (below). They want an evidence bundle by EOD tomorrow. Quick asks:

1) Irene, can you produce the HSM attestation PDF and the last 12 months of rotation logs (CSV) with rotation event IDs and a short README explaining the columns?
2) Marissa, please pull the KMS audit export (create/get/wrap/unwrap) and redact any user principals that are GCP/Cloud provider-managed keys; include a mapping file showing redaction mapping.
3) Sean, gather the TLS/transit proof: cipher list from our LB, confirmation of mTLS usage for internal node-to-node traffic, and any blurbs on TLS termination for hosted API.

I'll assemble into a single bundle and send to Helix. If anything is sensitive, mark it and we'll provide a redacted version plus a control narrative. Attach: quick checklist I prepared (evidence-checklist-helix.txt).

Deadlines: internal by 2pm PT today so I can validate and send by EOD.\
Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Vanessa / team — attaching the bundle we discussed. Attachment stubs below: redwood_hsm_attestation_2028-11-Helix.pdf, kms_rotation_log_apr2029.csv, kms_audit_export_2029-03.tar.gz, transit_tls_cipherlist_2029-04.txt, byok_handshake_summary.md.

Quick summary for the auditor (copy this into the control narrative):

- HSM & attestation: We use Thales Luna 7 Series (Luna HSM 7) hosted in our Dedicated HSM zone. Latest vendor attestation: FIPS 140-2 Level 3, attested 2028-11-10. The attestation PDF includes serials and validation stamps.

- Key storage & envelope encryption: Customer data keys (DEKs) are AES-256-GCM. DEKs are wrapped (key-encryption keys, KEKs) with the HSM using RSA-OAEP-2048 for cross-region wrap operations and local AES-KW for internal rotations. We maintain an envelope encryption pattern — payload encrypted with DEK, DEK wrapped by KMS-managed KEK inside HSM.

- Rotation policy & logs: Primary KEKs rotate quarterly; DEKs are rotated per retention/workload policy on-demand. Attached kms_rotation_log_apr2029.csv includes event_id, key_label_hash (hashed), rotation_timestamp_utc, actor_principal, pre_rotation_thumbprint, post_rotation_thumbprint, and rotation_reason. We cryptographically hash key identifiers in exports to avoid exposing raw key material.

- Audit exports: kms_audit_export_2029-03.tar.gz contains the access events (create/get/wrap/unwrap) for March 2029. We retain KMS event logs for 7 years to meet SOC2 requirements; exports are integrity-signed and include a manifest file with sha256 digests.

- Transit encryption: Our public API uses TLS 1.3 with cipher suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384. mTLS is enforced between internal service mesh endpoints; LB TLS termination is handled in our edge fleet with short-lived certs from our internal CA. Attachment transit_tls_cipherlist_2029-04.txt includes the exact cipher list and LB termination notes.

- BYOK workflow: We support customer key import via a signed handshake. byok_handshake_summary.md contains the handshake steps, verification checks, and an example CSR exchange (no private key material). For BYOK, we provide ephemeral wrapping of imported key material inside a customer-specific workspace HSM partition.

- Access & emergency procedures: The kms_access_matrix is included inside the audit bundle (redacted) and shows role-to-action mapping (KEY_ADMIN, CRYPTO_OPS, AUDIT_READ). Break-glass requests are time-limited and require 2-of-3 approvers from Security and Ops; each event is logged with justification and post-mortem.

Notes on redaction: Where principal names might expose internal usernames, we replace with consistent pseudonyms in the exported CSV and include a mapping file for the auditor under NDA.

If Helix's security team needs a live walkthrough of an HSM attestation or a time-windowed read access, we can arrange a 30-minute session with Ops.

— Irene Choi
Irene Choi | Director, Applied Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia / Helix SOC team —

Thanks for the list. We've attached an evidence bundle and brief control narrative addressing the items you requested: HSM attestation, rotation logs (hashed IDs), audit exports, transit cipher lists, and our BYOK handshake summary. A couple of notes:

- Certain access principals in the audit export have been pseudonymized; we included a mapping file under NDA.
- HSM attestation includes vendor serials; if you need on-site validation we can schedule a short session with our Ops lead.
- Rotation logs include cryptographic thumbprints rather than raw key material; this is by design for export safety.

If you'd like a 30-minute walk-through with Irene and Sean to review any artifact, propose a time and we'll confirm.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
